title: Evaluation dataset generator
purpose: This subsystem is a fully offline, stdlib-only pipeline that automatically builds evaluation benchmark datasets for the RAG chatbot: it parses the knowledge-base Markdown documents, classifies each document into one of 9 domain categories, synthesizes natural conversational question-answer pairs from the sections using 8 simulated helpdesk personas, then validates, deduplicates, and writes the results to per-category JSON files in evaluation/datasets/. The generated datasets are the QA ground-truth consumed by the evaluation benchmark runners (evaluation/benchmarks/evaluator.py, benchmark.py, retrieval_benchmark.py) to score retrieval and answering quality of the campus helpdesk RAG stack.

files.purpose: Package marker that documents the dataset generator's scope (parse -> classify -> synthesize -> validate -> deduplicate -> write) and declares the package version.

terms.definition: A structured JSON file of (question, expected_answer) QA pairs used as ground truth to score the RAG chatbot; generated per category into evaluation/datasets/.

files.notes: Only a docstring and __version__ = "0.1.0"; contains no importable logic.

files.purpose: Defines AnswerExtractor, which strips Markdown formatting from a section's content and returns a grounded verbatim/excerpted answer snippet limited to that section.

terms.definition: An answer excerpt whose text must contain content from the source section (a grounding check fails the extraction), preventing invented or cross-file-polluted answers.

files.notes: DEAD CODE: AnswerExtractor is not imported by pipeline.py or any other module in this package (verified by search). The pipeline instead synthesizes expected_answer inline in question_generator.py and grounds it via DatasetValidator, so extract_answer's stricter section-only grounding is never exercised.

files.purpose: Defines CategoryClassifier, which assigns each parsed Markdown document to one of the 9 target categories by scoring path keywords (weight 5.0/4.0), title/heading keyword hits (3.0), and content keyword frequency (0.5 per hit).

terms.definition: Heuristic assignment of each document to a domain bucket (Admission, Departments, Hostel, Fees, Placement, Navigation, Facilities, Faculty, Misc) via weighted path/keyword scoring; scores below 2.0 default to Misc.
The per-category keyword lists from config (category_keywords) used to detect domain signals in titles, headings, and document content.

files.notes: Misc is a bucket category: its keyword rule set is absent from category_keywords (the dict covers 8 real categories), and Misc is excluded from best-category selection until the threshold fallback. Path heuristics are hardcoded strings (e.g. 'admission', 'hostel') rather than data-driven.

files.purpose: Defines the GeneratorConfig dataclass holding all pipeline defaults: input/output directories, per-doc question count bounds, answer length limits, dedup threshold, the 9 category set, category->JSON filename mapping, 8 helpdesk personas, and per-category keyword lists.

terms.definition: One of 8 simulated real-world helpdesk user roles (e.g. newly admitted student, parent accompanying student, student lost on campus) that question phrasing is authored from.
Mapping from category name to the JSON dataset filename it is written to (e.g. 'Admission' -> admission.json).

files.notes: No config.yaml / .env / environment variables are read anywhere in this package; all configuration is dataclass defaults plus CLI overrides in pipeline.py. words_per_question=80 drives the target question count. overwrite_existing defaults to True here, but the CLI's --overwrite flag is store_true (default False), so behavior differs between direct-construction and CLI invocation.

files.purpose: Defines SemanticDeduplicator, which removes exact and near-duplicate questions from candidate lists using normalized-string comparison, length-difference fast exit, Jaccard token-set similarity, and difflib SequenceMatcher ratio against a configurable threshold (default 0.85).

terms.definition: Similarity ratio (default 0.85) above which two candidate queries are treated as duplicates and dropped; applied to Jaccard and SequenceMatcher scores.
Intersection-over-union of the token sets of two normalized queries, used as one of four near-duplicate detection signals.

files.notes: O(n^2) pairwise comparison over accumulated seen queries; acceptable for small batches but quadratic in the number of candidates. Empty normalized queries are counted as removed. Pipeline also runs a second, string-exact per-category dedup (seen_q) before writing.

files.purpose: Standalone CLI utility that pretty-prints 20 (configurable) sample records from each generated dataset JSON file in evaluation/datasets/ for manual quality inspection.
files.notes: Dev-only tool, not part of the pipeline. Emits non-ASCII emoji in console output (❌) which can break on some Windows code pages. Prints expected_answer truncated to 120 chars.

files.purpose: Defines the DatasetGeneratorPipeline orchestrator plus a CLI entry point (main/parse_args) that runs the whole flow: discover Markdown, parse, classify, generate, validate, deduplicate per file, re-dedup per category, write datasets, and print a summary report.

terms.definition: Scoring the retrieval-augmented chatbot against generated ground-truth QA datasets; the CLI help labels this generator as the tooling that produces those benchmark inputs.

config: CLI args: --input-dir (default data/processed_docs), --output-dir (default evaluation/datasets), --min-questions (5), --max-questions (20), --dedup-threshold (0.85), --overwrite (store_true, default False), --verbose
files.notes: Adds workspace root to sys.path when run as a script, so both `python -m evaluation.dataset_generator.pipeline` and direct execution work. Hardcodes legacy fallback dirs (bvbcet_rag_pipeline/knowledge_base/markdown, bvbcet_rag_pipeline/markdown, archive/bvbcet_rag_pipeline/knowledge_base/markdown) used only if the configured input_dir is empty. Sets doc.metadata['assigned_category'] which QuestionGenerator later reads - implicit coupling across modules. --overwrite default (False) contradicts GeneratorConfig.overwrite_existing default (True). average_questions_per_doc guards against divide-by-zero.

files.purpose: Defines the GeneratedQuestionCandidate dataclass and QuestionGenerator, which computes a target question count per document, then synthesizes persona-tagged, category-specific conversational questions from each section with difficulty and keyword metadata.

terms.definition: A synthesized QA pair (question, expected_answer, section_heading, perspective, difficulty, keywords) before validation/dedup.
A coarse easy/medium/hard label hardcoded per generated question template.
The cleaned human-readable name (from document title or section heading) that gets interpolated into templated questions, e.g. 'the Computer Science department'.

files.notes: Questions come from hardcoded per-category template lists, not from the LLM; category templates only for Admission, Navigation, Departments, Hostel, Facilities, Fees, Placement, Faculty, and a generic else branch. expected_answer is simply the first sentence of the section (not the AnswerExtractor). Deterministic sampling: random.seed(42) then random.sample. Sections shorter than 25 chars, or whose heading starts with 'pdf document:'/'source:', are skipped. No documents/sections are queried via the embedding/BM25 infrastructure - this is template generation only.

files.purpose: Defines the SectionBlock and MarkdownDocument dataclasses and MarkdownReader, which recursively discovers .md files and parses them into a title, heading list, and hierarchical section blocks.

terms.definition: A heading + level + the content lines following it up to the next heading; the unit questions are generated from.
Structured in-memory representation of one parsed Markdown file: path, filename, title, headings, sections, metadata, word counts, raw content.

files.notes: Heading regex is '^(#{1,6})\s+(.+)$'; content before the first heading is grouped under the document title. Title = first '# ' heading, else file stem title-cased with underscores replaced by spaces. Reads with errors='ignore' (silently drops undecodable bytes). metadata stores only relative_path; pipeline appends assigned_category. Returns None for empty/unreadable files.

files.purpose: Defines DatasetValidator, which filters candidate QA pairs by question/answer length limits, keyword groundedness against the source document (>=60% of answer keywords must appear), and generic/ambiguous question patterns.

terms.definition: Check that >=60% of the answer's significant keywords (>3 chars) appear in the raw source document text; below that the answer is rejected as ungrounded/hallucinated.

files.notes: Rejection reasons are returned as the second tuple element ('Empty question text', 'Question too short', 'Answer length below minimum', 'Ungrounded answer', 'Ambiguous generic question pattern'). The 60% ratio check only runs if the answer yields non-empty keywords.

files.purpose: Defines DatasetWriter, which formats validated candidates into the record schema (id, question, expected_answer, expected_document, category, section, source_heading, keywords, difficulty, perspective) and merges/appends them into per-category JSON dataset files.

terms.definition: The JSON object shape written to dataset files, matching what the benchmark runners (evaluator.py, benchmark.py, retrieval_benchmark.py) read as QA ground truth.

config: config.overwrite_existing (True if new writes replace existing files instead of merging)
files.notes: With overwrite_existing=True, existing records are discarded and IDs restart at 1; with False (the CLI default), it loads existing records and continues IDs. Writes UTF-8 with indent=2, ensure_ascii=False. Duplicate 'id' collisions are possible across runs when merging records that were also deduplicated by question string. 'expected_document' is just doc.filename (basename), not the full relative path.

data_flow: Entry point is evaluation/dataset_generator/pipeline.py, runnable as a module or script (it injects the workspace root into sys.path). No other subsystem imports this package; it is an offline batch tool invoked manually/CLI. Input: knowledge-base Markdown discovered recursively under data/processed_docs (with hardcoded fallbacks to legacy dirs bvbcet_rag_pipeline/knowledge_base/markdown, bvbcet_rag_pipeline/markdown, archive/bvbcet_rag_pipeline/knowledge_base/markdown if empty). Flow: MarkdownReader parses files into MarkdownDocument -> CategoryClassifier assigns a category (stored in doc.metadata['assigned_category']) -> QuestionGenerator emits GeneratedQuestionCandidates per section -> DatasetValidator filters by quality/groundedness -> SemanticDeduplicator removes near-duplicates per file -> writer merges per-category JSON files in evaluation/datasets/*.json (admission.json ... misc.json), re-deduping by exact question string per category. Output: one JSON list per category of records with id/question/expected_answer/expected_document/category/section/source_heading/keywords/difficulty/perspective. Downstream consumers are the evaluation benchmark runners, which default their dataset_dir to evaluation/datasets: evaluation/benchmarks/evaluator.py, evaluation/benchmarks/benchmark.py, evaluation/benchmarks/retrieval_benchmark.py (and scripts/benchmark.py). inspect_dataset.py reads the same JSON files for manual QA.
external_deps: Python 3.11 standard library only: argparse, dataclasses, difflib, json, logging, math, random, re, sys, time, pathlib, typing, collections.defaultdict. No third-party packages, no Ollama/LLM, no embedding models.
risks: answer_extractor.py is dead code: AnswerExtractor is never imported or called by the pipeline; the pipeline substitutes a weaker inline extraction (first sentence of section) and keyword-ratio grounding, so the stricter section-only grounding guarantee is not enforced.

Config drift: GeneratorConfig.overwrite_existing defaults to True but the CLI --overwrite flag defaults to False, so a direct-construction run replaces dataset files while a CLI run merges them - identical pipeline, different merge semantics.

Question/answer quality is bounded by hardcoded templates: questions are templated per category with the entity name interpolated and expected_answer is just the section's first sentence; there is no semantic check that a question actually targets the answer. The 8 personas and all templates are static lists in code, so generated variety is limited.

No cross-document dedup of meaning: dedup is per-file (SemanticDeduplicator) plus per-category exact-string; semantically identical questions phrased slightly differently across documents (e.g. two 'Where is the canteen?' variants) can both survive into the same dataset.

Groundedness is a loose keyword co-occurrence check (>=60% of >3-char answer keywords present anywhere in the raw document), so answers can still mismatch their labeled section/category or contain keywords scattered across the document.

Fallback dirs and path-heuristic classification are hardcoded to legacy bvbcet_rag_pipeline paths; classification is purely heuristic string scoring with no LLM or structured metadata, so miscategorized documents silently land in Misc.

The generator does not use the actual retrieval stack (no embedding/BM25/FAISS); expected_answer provenance is document text only, so datasets cannot validate cross-document or retrieval-position-dependent behavior.
